clue.text: Host regularly entertaining republic's next in line

indicators.note: to entertain is to hold within, so the alternate letters go round the country
taking every other letter of the word Host, its first and third

parts.note: Eire, the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland, with its possessive S

explanation.surface: A host periodically entertaining the heir to some republic's leadership.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the first and third letters of Host; 'entertaining' wraps them round the Irish republic's name. 'Host' looks like the definition but only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A female heir is the person standing next in line to inherit an estate or title.

clue.text: Pole possibly curtailed residence, saving cash out East

indicators.note: to save is to keep in, so the money goes within the residence
curtailed means the tail, the last letter, is cut off

parts.note: home is a residence

indicators.note: the East letter is taken out of the money word

parts.note: money is cash
E is the compass abbreviation for East

explanation.surface: A Polish person cuts back on housing, keeping cash outside the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'curtailed' trims the residence word, 'out' drops East from the cash word, and 'saving' tucks that inside. 'Pole' is not a nationality: pole and poll sound alike.
explanation.definitionFit: Words of identical sound or spelling with different meanings, like pole and poll, are examples of this term.

clue.text: Popular act, say, taking extremists in Europe prisoner

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular

indicators.note: say marks a word that sounds like another

parts.note: a turn is a stage act

indicators.note: the extreme letters of the word Europe, first and last

explanation.surface: A popular performer takes some European extremists prisoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' turns TURN into the sound-alike TERN; 'extremists in' gives EE.
explanation.definitionFit: An internee is someone confined as a prisoner, especially in wartime.

clue.text: Treacherous person loses head, requiring firm support

indicators.note: a head is the top or front, so losing it means the first letter of the treacherous word drops away

parts.note: a weasel is a sly, treacherous person

explanation.surface: A traitor is beheaded and has to be held up firmly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses head' drops the W of WEASEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An easel is a sturdy stand that holds up an artist's canvas.

clue.text: Vessel with shy cat wandering around

indicators.note: the rearranged letters go around the joining word
wandering letters stray into a new order

parts.note: and means with

explanation.surface: A boat carrying a timid cat that roams about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wandering' rearranges SHY CAT to SYACHT; 'around' puts it round AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand yacht is a wheeled land craft with a sail, called a vessel by extension.

clue.text: Shoots game

definitions.meaning: to shoot is to move suddenly and fast, as a fish shoots through water
a pub game of throwing small arrows at a board

explanation.definitionFit: The verb sense is to move swiftly, and the noun is the British pub game played with flighted missiles at a dartboard.

clue.text: Break up, having mistakenly set précis

parts.note: to dig is to break up soil

indicators.note: mistakenly means the word set appears in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Wrongly arranged, the summary falls apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' rearranges SET to EST.
explanation.definitionFit: A digest is a condensed summary, the same thing as a précis.

clue.text: Male sappers adopting US soldier's course of treatment

indicators.note: taking in, so the soldier goes inside

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, whose soldiers are called sappers
men as in male people
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: Army engineers take in an American soldier for medical treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'adopting' takes the American soldier inside the Royal Engineers' men; sappers are military engineers.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of diet, exercise or medical treatment.

clue.text: It's a sound bet, the entrecote!

indicators.note: sound here describes how a word is pronounced, not how safe it is

parts.note: a stake is a bet

explanation.surface: Claiming the sirloin is a safe wager.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sound bet' suggests a safe wager; 'sound' is the signal that STAKE sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Entrecote is a cut of beef from between the ribs, i.e. a type of steak.

clue.text: Not quite notice archer on round tower

indicators.note: not quite means the final letter is missing

parts.note: to mark is to notice
William Tell, the legendary Swiss archer
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An archer is barely spotted on top of a round tower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not quite' trims the last letter of the notice word. A Martello is a round coastal fort built in Britain against Napoleon.
explanation.definitionFit: A Martello is a small round defensive tower, many built on English coasts.

clue.text: Allow old currency into island

indicators.note: the currency goes inside the island word

parts.note: an ait is a small river island, as on the Thames
DM, the Deutschmark, Germany's currency before the euro

explanation.surface: Permitting a former currency to be used on an island.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to admit someone is to allow them entry, or to allow a claim as true.

clue.text: Worshippers keen to terminate wrongdoing, we hear

indicators.note: signals that the words are judged by how they sound when spoken, not by spelling

parts.note: wrongdoing is SIN, and keen (AGOG) comes at its end to close it off

explanation.surface: Churchgoers eager to put a stop to bad behaviour.
explanation.walkthrough: SIN followed by AGOG, said together, sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a Jewish congregation as well as its building, so it can stand for a body of worshippers.

clue.text: Taken in by brief warbling, aim and shoot

indicators.note: the aim word is taken into the shortened singing word
brief means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: a trill is a warbling run of notes
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: Hearing short bursts of birdsong, a hunter takes aim and fires.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' drops the last letter of the warbling word, and 'Taken in by' puts the aim word inside it. 'shoot' looks like a verb with 'aim', but it is a plant's shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanical sense: a tendril is a slender climbing shoot of a plant.

clue.text: Veil terribly shaky old woman carried

indicators.note: the old woman is carried within the rearranged letters
terribly marks the word shaky as letters to be rearranged

parts.note: informal for mother, ma

explanation.surface: A veil worn by an old woman who is trembling badly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terribly' scrambles the shaky letters and 'carried' takes the old woman inside them, between the fourth and fifth letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A yashmak is a veil worn by some Muslim women in public to cover the face.

clue.text: North American feller, one who isn't all right on land

definitions.meaning: one who fells trees in the forests of Canada and the US

definitions.text: one who isn't all right on land
definitions.meaning: a jack (sailor) who lumbers clumsily ashore

explanation.walkthrough: 'feller' is not a chap but someone who fells; JACK is crossword slang for a sailor, who lumbers on dry land.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is a North American woodcutter; the second is a whimsical sailor who walks awkwardly ashore.

clue.text: We lark about with bird, one taking risks on road

parts.note: a jay is a bird of the crow family

indicators.note: about means the words are shuffled round

explanation.surface: We fool around with a bird, someone taking chances on the road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges WE LARK to WALKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaywalker crosses the road carelessly, against traffic rules, risking injury.

clue.text: Ignoring husband, consider backing contract

indicators.note: backing means the remaining letters run backwards
the husband letter is left out of the word

parts.note: to think is to consider

explanation.surface: Without her husband, she weighs up supporting a contract.
explanation.walkthrough: THINK without H gives TINK; 'backing' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit the brows is to contract or draw them together, as in a frown.

clue.text: It may bring word of obstruction over border rising

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the whole run of letters reads upwards
in a down entry, over puts the obstruction word on top of the border word

parts.note: marge is an old word for a border or edge
a let is an obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance'

explanation.surface: A message delivered over a blockaded frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: LET over MARGE read upwards: 'rising' reverses the pair, giving TEL then EGRAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A telegram was a printed message delivered by hand, so it brings word.

clue.text: Suspend start of play, changing sides at one point

indicators.note: at one place the left letter swaps for the right letter

parts.note: a prologue is the opening of a play

explanation.surface: Halt the opening of a play while teams swap ends at some stage.
explanation.walkthrough: L (left) becomes R (right).
explanation.definitionFit: To prorogue Parliament is to suspend its sitting without dissolving it.

clue.text: River put to some purpose by duck

indicators.note: the zero sits by, i.e. next to, the purpose word

parts.note: a duck is a score of nought in cricket, so the letter O
use means purpose, as in 'to no use'

explanation.surface: A river being made useful by a duck.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ouse is the name of several English rivers, notably the one flowing through York.

clue.text: Administer clubs in school — but screw up!

indicators.note: these pieces go inside the school abbreviation

parts.note: to run is to administer
C is the card suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Running golf clubs in a school, but making a mess of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrunch paper is to crumple it, i.e. screw it up.

clue.text: Riley chats disjointedly, being overwrought

indicators.note: the words come apart and are put together in a new order

explanation.surface: Riley talks in fragments, too worked up to make sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disjointedly' rearranges RILEY plus CHATS.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: being overwrought means being in an uncontrolled emotional state.

clue.text: Like faction caught disclosing secrets verbally?

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: verbally means spoken, so the word is matched by its sound

parts.note: leaky means prone to letting out secrets

explanation.surface: A faction caught giving away secrets by word of mouth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'verbally' makes LEAKY stand for its sound-alike LIQUEY.
explanation.definitionFit: Cliquey means relating to a clique, a small exclusive group or faction.

clue.text: Gloomy youth upset about unspecified doctrine

indicators.note: the turned youth word goes around the doctrine
upset in a down entry means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: a lad is a youth
an ism is any unnamed doctrine

explanation.surface: A gloomy young man upset over some ideology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns LAD to DAL, which goes 'about' ISM.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: dismal means gloomy, depressing.

clue.text: Piano a singer installed in artist's suite

parts.note: P is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly

indicators.note: the bird is placed inside the artist abbreviation

parts.note: RA, a Royal Academician, a stock crossword artist
a tit is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A soft-voiced singer is set up in a painter's apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: A partita is a Baroque instrumental suite of dance movements.

clue.text: Old dog going without tea

indicators.note: going outside, so the dog wraps the old letter

parts.note: a peke is a Pekingese dog

explanation.surface: An ageing dog goes without its cuppa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'going without' means going outside, not lacking.
explanation.definitionFit: Pekoe is a high-quality black tea from Sri Lanka or India.

clue.text: Pet given last of cordial in bottle

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the courage word

parts.note: bottle is British slang for courage or daring

indicators.note: takes the final letter of the word cordial

explanation.surface: A pet animal given the dregs of a cordial in a bottle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' is not a container: it is British slang for nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: A darling is a beloved person, and pet is used the same affectionate way.

clue.text: Ancient dialect in Greenland or Iceland

indicators.note: in marks the answer lying within the words that follow

explanation.surface: An old way of speaking found in Greenland or Iceland.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across greenlanD OR ICeland.
explanation.definitionFit: Doric was the dialect of ancient Greek spoken by the Dorians, e.g. in Sparta.

clue.text: Warwick ruler manufacturer?

definitions.meaning: the Earl of Warwick, called the ... in the Wars of the Roses
one who makes rulers, i.e. monarchs, not measuring sticks

explanation.walkthrough: 'ruler' suggests a measuring stick; here it is a monarch. Richard Neville, Earl of Warwick, earned the nickname by deposing and installing English kings.
explanation.definitionFit: Historical nickname of Warwick, and literally someone who makes a monarch.

clue.text: A boxer about to consume high-class cheese?

indicators.note: the reversed letters eat, i.e. take inside, the next piece
about means turned round, so the pair of words reads backwards

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog
U is the stock abbreviation for upper-class

explanation.surface: A prizefighter is about to tuck into some posh cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses A DOG to GODA; 'to consume' puts U inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Gouda is a mild yellow Dutch cheese named after its home town.

clue.text: Radical youth leader originally pursuing the unruly

indicators.note: the initials follow behind the rearranged letters
unruly marks the word the as letters that misbehave and rearrange
originally means at the start, so the first letters of youth and leader

explanation.surface: An extremist young leader first chases after the disorderly mob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unruly' rearranges THE to ETH; 'originally' gives Y and L.
explanation.definitionFit: In chemistry a radical is a group of atoms acting as a unit; ethyl is one such group.

clue.text: Part of garden Marciano planted without hesitation

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the boxer's name goes round

parts.note: Rocky Marciano, the US world heavyweight boxing champion
er is a hesitant sound

explanation.surface: Part of the garden planted by a famous boxer without pause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' does not mean lacking: it means outside, so the boxer's first name wraps the hesitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A rockery is a garden feature of stones planted with alpines.
